items.followUp: How do qualitative and quantitative data differ? Give one example of each.

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics rather than numerical measurements.
rubric.description: States that qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics and are non-numerical.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying qualitative observations as descriptive or non-numerical.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations involve measurements or counts expressed numerically.
rubric.description: States that quantitative observations use numerical measurements or counts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying quantitative observations as numerical measurements or counts.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics without using numbers.
Quantitative observations involve measurements or counts and are expressed numerically.

items.followUp: State two observations made by A. F. A. King that supported a connection between mosquitoes and malaria.

rubric.why: King observed that malaria was common in areas where mosquitoes were abundant, including marshy areas.
rubric.description: Gives the observation that malaria was common where mosquitoes were abundant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation, including the association between malaria and abundant mosquitoes or marshy areas.

rubric.why: King observed that people sleeping outdoors were more likely to contract malaria than those sleeping indoors.
rubric.description: Gives the observation comparing malaria risk among people sleeping outdoors and indoors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation or a clear equivalent comparison.

modelAnswer: Malaria was common in areas where mosquitoes were abundant, such as marshy places.
People who slept outdoors were more likely to contract malaria than people who slept indoors.

items.followUp: What are the functions of chromoplasts and leucoplasts?

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to plant parts.
rubric.description: Defines a chromoplast as a plastid containing coloured pigments or one that gives colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its pigments or colour-imparting role.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids and commonly store food.
rubric.description: Defines a leucoplast as a colourless plastid or states its food-storage role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as colourless or mentioning food storage.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are plastids containing coloured pigments other than chlorophyll, which give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that commonly store food.
